items.title: Telangana govt forms panel to modernise polytechnic education after student protests
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Telangana government on Monday, August 24, constituted a six-member high-level committee to examine the future of polytechnic education after students protested over the proposed integration of polytechnic education with the Young India Skills University (YISU). The panel will be headed by Adviser (Public Affairs) K Keshava Rao and include MLC M Kodandaram, former National Commission for Protection of Child Rights chairperson Shanta Sinha, Special Chief Secretary (Energy) Navin Mittal, Secretary of the SHAKTI (Department of Skill Human Capital and Knowledge Training Initiatives) Department Hari Chandana Dasari and Commissioner of Technical Education A Devasena. The committee has been asked to hold consultations with students, faculty and other stakeholders, examine the concerns surrounding the proposed changes and submit specific recommendations within 30 days. The government will take further action based on its findings. items.title: Doesn't deserve to be public prosecutor: Supreme Court on TN law officer who withheld key evidence
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday sought the Tamil Nadu government’s response to strong remarks made by the Madras High Court against a public prosecutor who failed to place crucial evidence before the trial court in a rape case. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta issued notice on a challenge by the public prosecutor against the observations made by the High Court in its order. However, while doing so, it questioned the prosecutor's credibility for failing to produce an accident register before the trial court despite the register being part of his case diary. The register contained details of the injuries suffered by the rape victim. "He does not deserve to be a public prosecutor. Such a vital document you withheld. It was available in your case diary. May be technically you may be right that no notice was given but you don't deserve any notice, as a matter of fact. You don't deserve to be a public prosecutor." the Court said. items.summary: The tiger has a place both in the artwork of India’s original Constitution and in maintaining the country’s ecological balance, Union Minister of State for Law and Justice (Independent Charge) Arjun Ram Meghwal said on Saturday. Meghwal was speaking at the launch of Sacred Tiger Tales: From Vedic Hymns to Tryst with Stripes , authored and photographed by senior Law Ministry official Manoj Kumar. The 248-page coffee-table book, published by OakBridge Publishing, was unveiled by Meghwal alongside Attorney Genera l R Venkataramani at the India International Centre in New Delhi. The book features 82 short narratives spanning scripture, classical literature, folklore, colonial history, and modern conservation, alongside photographs taken across Indian tiger reserves. items.title: Andhra HC tells state govt to ensure all clearances for Google-Adani data centre
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Andhra Pradesh High Court on Monday, August 24, directed the state government to ensure that construction of the proposed USD 15-billion Google-Adani data-centre project in Visakhapatnam is carried out only after obtaining all necessary legal and environmental permissions. A bench headed by Chief Justice Lisa Gill issued the direction while hearing a petition challenging various approvals granted for the project. The court did not accept the petitioner's request for an interim status quo, which would have halted work at the site. Instead, it asked the government to ensure that construction complies with all applicable regulations. The court also directed the state to file a consolidated response from the departments involved in granting approvals. The matter is expected to come up again next week. The petition, filed by Bolisetty Satyanarayana, raises several concerns about the project, including the use of around 160 acres of land belonging to Simhachalam Devasthanam. items.title: TN women MLAs object to use of ‘kanni pechu’ for maiden speeches in Assembly
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK) floor leader Sowmiya Anbumani and Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] MLA T Latha on Monday, August 24, urged the Tamil Nadu Assembly to stop using the term ‘ kanni pechu ’ to refer to an MLA’s maiden speech, saying the expression has patriarchal connotations. They suggested using ‘arimuga urai’ (introductory speech) or ‘ mudhal urai’ (first speech) instead. The issue was raised during a debate on the demands for grants for the Education and Municipal Administration departments. The discussion came up after Usilampatti Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA M Vijay alleged that the previous Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) government was responsible for the water crisis in his constituency. When DMK members attempted to intervene during Vijay's speech, members of the Treasury Benches asked them to allow him to continue, referring to it as his ‘kanni pechu ’ — his maiden speech. Objecting to the expression, Sowmiya said the term should be avoided and suggested that the House use ‘arimuga urai’ or ‘muthal urai’ instead.
